description:
637 tiles at 16x16 for a hangar bay, a command deck and an engineering space: deck plating, shielded reactor plate, hangar floor, bright alloy decking, non-slip tread plate, faced bulkheads and cable conduit — with the cast a station is recognised by, from cargo containers and fuel drums to a reactor core housing, coolant tanks, console banks, EVA suits and airlock hatches. Commercial use permitted, in unlimited projects, with no attribution required; the one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the pack itself.

Importers for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled and Godot ship in the download, and each was run by the engine it targets and made to count what it built.

What is in the download

  • 470 of the 637 tiles are transitions, 74% of the pack. 10 complete 47-mask autotile sets: every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single. Completeness is checked mechanically on every build, because a set missing three tiles is broken in your map.
  • The bulkhead caps into whichever deck it stands on. That is the detail the pack exists for. A hull plate does not meet a hangar floor the way it meets reactor plate — so there is a bulkhead set per deck rather than one bulkhead reused: standing out of the deck plating, out of the hangar floor, and out of engineering's reactor plate. Bright alloy decking is laid into each of those three the same way, as a loading pad, a service island or a command deck, and the decks meet each other directly: hangar to plating, reactor to plating, tread gratings let into both.
  • A bulkhead that reads as a bulkhead: a lit lip along the top of its face, a cap on the north and west shoulders where the light strikes, and a shadow cast onto the deck in front of it. Every tile of every bulkhead set is declared impassable in tiles.json, because a bulkhead is walked into rather than along.
  • 8 materials × 4 variants on a value ladder laid out before any art existed, so the station does not collapse into one undifferentiated flat grey. The smallest gap on the ladder is 16.7 luma, measured from the shipped pixels rather than declared.
  • 27 objects across 71 tiles. The hangar bay: a cargo container, crate stacks, fuel drums, a deck beacon, and the guide chevrons and hazard striping that were kept OUT of the floor fill so your map places them where the traffic actually goes. Engineering: a reactor core housing, coolant tanks, a pipe manifold, valve wheels, a power cell rack and an air scrubber. The command deck: a console bank, a holo table and chart screens. The crew spaces: bunks, lockers, a mess table, a hydroponics tray and a water tank. The airlock: an EVA suit rack, a hatch with its wheel and a tool locker. Each ships transparent, and grounded on the deck it belongs to with the contact shadow already drawn.
  • 4 animated objects, 64 frames: a scanner dish sweeping its face, a coolant line running up its sight glass, a status board scrolling and filling, and an extractor fan turning. The silhouette holds still; only the sweep, the flow, the readout and the blades move, and no two frames of a set are the same picture.
  • A finished 40x28 sample map with 199 objects on it and every autotile set placed, as a PNG, as JSON naming every cell by tile id, and as a .tmx that opens in Tiled.
  • 32 4x4 proof renders, one per repeating tile, so you can look for the grid line yourself.
  • Every tile as a loose PNG and as packed sheets: 740 files in total, and a tiles.json giving every tile's role, material, sheet slot, footprint and passability.

Two things to know before you buy

⚠️ The animation plays in Tiled and Godot, not in RPG Maker MZ. MZ animates tiles only through its A1 page, which holds animated water autotiles; this pack has none, so in MZ the animated objects arrive as static frames on page D.

⚠️ The conduit is drawn, not animated. The two cable runs are fill tiles: a trunk laid along a deck, with no transition set and no rung on the value ladder, because a run laid on a deck is not a deck. They are left passable, because trunking is stepped over, and a map that wants a particular run solid can block those cells itself. If you want a live line, the coolant_flow animation is the object that carries motion.

The importers were actually run

  • RPG Maker MZ: an A2 autotile sheet (the page MZ's own autotile brush paints) plus B/C/D object pages and a slot map. It composes correctly against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE: 10 of 10 sets, 470 of 470 masked tiles, and 480 of 480 shapes came back byte-identical. The object pages carry every fill, every object and every animation frame.
  • Tiled: one .tsx per group, all 14 opened and rendered by Tiled 1.12.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared pixel for pixel with the shipped sheets: 712 sheet cells, 0 differing. The sample map's .tmx renders 1,146,880 pixels identical to the shipped PNG.
  • Godot 4: a .tres TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2: 14 atlas sources, 637 of 637 declared tiles built, 30 of 30 multi-cell footprints exact. Every sheet is referenced by a relative filename, so the folder loads from wherever you put it in a project.

What is proven, and what is not

The grid is exact, the palette is locked to 49 colours, the alpha is strictly binary with no anti-aliasing, every tile carries a declared role, and every autotile set is complete: exact checks, run on every build.

Seamlessness is not on that list. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed; grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven. The renders ship with the pack so you can judge them yourself.

The autotile sets

It fits the rest of the series

The 16x16 Verdant packs are drawn at one cell size in one style, so this station sits beside the others and a corridor can run straight out of it into another pack.

  • Verdant 11 — Vessel — the ship that docks at the hangar, on the same grid and the same palette
  • Verdant 14 — Institutional Interiors — offices, corridors and meeting rooms, for the station's admin and crew decks
  • Verdant 22 — Sewers — pipework and service tunnels, for the levels under the reactor deck

AI disclosure

Tagged as AI-assisted. Precisely: every tile is drawn by a procedural generator written for this series, and that generator's code was written with AI assistance. No diffusion model is anywhere in the tile pipeline. Every image on this page, the cover included, is composed from the pack's own tiles and sample map.
